title: GitHub Actions Examples
description: Small GitHub Actions examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: A workflow file
examples.description: A workflow describes jobs GitHub Actions can run for a repository. The YAML file lives under .github/workflows.
examples.code:
name: Say hello
on: workflow_dispatch
jobs:
  hello:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "Hello, club"

examples.title: Events start workflows
examples.description: An event tells GitHub when to consider running a workflow. workflow_dispatch is manual; push reacts to selected pushed changes.

examples.title: Jobs and steps
examples.description: A job runs a list of steps on a runner. Steps in one job run in order and share that job's working environment.
examples.code:
jobs:
  explain:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: First step
        run: echo "Read"
      - name: Second step
        run: echo "Check"

examples.title: Runners execute jobs
examples.description: A runner is the machine environment that executes a job. runs-on chooses a matching runner label.

examples.title: Name steps clearly
examples.description: Step names appear in the run log. Clear names help someone find the part that failed.
examples.code:
steps:
  - name: Show working directory
    run: pwd
  - name: Print learning message
    run: echo "Read the result"

examples.title: Environment values
examples.description: env gives a job or step named environment values. A shell can read them without repeating the literal text in each command.
examples.code:
env:
  CLUB_NAME: Reading club
steps:
  - run: echo "$CLUB_NAME"

examples.title: Job dependencies
examples.description: needs makes a job wait for another job to succeed. This states the order between jobs.
examples.code:
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "Check"
  report:
    needs: check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "Checks finished"

examples.title: Matrices repeat a job
examples.description: A matrix runs variations of a job. Each combination gets its own job run.
examples.code:
strategy:
  matrix:
    fruit: [apple, pear]
steps:
  - run: echo "${{ matrix.fruit }}"

examples.title: Limit token permissions
examples.description: The workflow token can be given small permissions. Give only the access a job actually needs.

examples.title: Handle untrusted text as data
examples.description: A workflow may receive text from a pull request. Do not paste untrusted text directly into a shell script; pass it as data and quote it.
examples.code:
env:
  NOTE: A fixed practice message
steps:
  - run: printf "%s\n" "$NOTE"

examples.title: Avoid duplicate obsolete runs
examples.description: Concurrency can group related runs. cancel-in-progress can stop an older run when a newer run in the same group starts.

examples.title: Read the run result
examples.description: A run log shows which jobs and steps completed. A green result means the configured commands passed, not that every product requirement was checked.
examples.code:
Check run:
  syntax check: passed
  unit tests: passed
  visual review: not part of this workflow
